<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"

    </bpmn:task>

      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_Gather_SelfAssessment</bpmn:outgoing>

    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_IdentifyGaps" name="Identify gaps or issues">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_Review_IdentifyGaps</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_IdentifyGaps_Correct</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_MakeCorrections" name="Make necessary corrections or improvements">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_IdentifyGaps_Correct</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_Correct_FinalAudit</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>

rules.instruction: When the description distinguishes preparatory work from a subsequent examination and states that findings are identified after the examination: model the examination as a distinct activity before the activity that identifies its findings
rules.situation: the description distinguishes preparatory work from a subsequent examination and states that findings are identified after the examination

rules.instruction: When the description explicitly states the outcome that terminates the process: Label the end event to reflect that stated outcome; do not use an unstated or different outcome.
rules.situation: the description states the outcome that terminates the process

rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant performs a distinct action to initiate the process: Model a start event for the process trigger, followed by a task for the initiating action; do not use the start event to represent the action itself.
rules.situation: the description says that an actor performs a distinct action to initiate the process

rules.instruction: When the description explicitly states what triggers the process or what outcome terminates it: Label the corresponding start or end event with a concise, faithful description of that stated trigger or outcome rather than a generic label.
rules.situation: the description states what initiates the process or what outcome terminates it
